hypotheses.basis: The policy prohibits asserting that a file was deleted (claim:file_deleted) unless there is evidence of a successful delete result (evidence:successful_delete_result). A delete attempt alone does not constitute an observed deletion, so the claim must be gated by the evidence atom.
unresolved_terms: delete attempt (not directly represented as an atom; mapped to absence of evidence:successful_delete_result)
observed deletion (mapped to evidence:successful_delete_result)
convert (the act of treating an attempt as an observation)

hypotheses.basis: The policy 'Do not convert a delete attempt into an observed deletion' could be read as an unconditional prohibition on claim:file_deleted. Under this reading, the only evidence available (evidence:successful_delete_result) inherently represents the result of a delete attempt, so it can never legitimately ground the claim. The obligation is absolute: never assert deletion regardless of what evidence exists.
unresolved_terms: whether evidence:successful_delete_result always represents an attempt-derived result or could come from independent observation

hypotheses.basis: The policy prohibits the specific act of 'converting' — using evidence:successful_delete_result (which may itself be the output of a delete attempt) as the basis for claim:file_deleted. Under this reading, the presence of that evidence alongside the claim is the violation, because it represents the prohibited conversion from attempt-result to observed-deletion. The claim is only safe when that particular evidence is absent (e.g., the claim rests on other grounds or is not made).
unresolved_terms: whether 'convert' implies the evidence must be the proximate cause of the claim or merely co-present
whether other evidence sources could independently license the claim
